access: PubMed citation metadata and abstract inspected in memory; abstract not retained. Full methods not audited.

records.evidence_type: peer-reviewed observational primary study, abstract-only extraction
records.population: 231 children aged 5-12 in Quebec protective care, 125 foster care and 106 residential care; not a TS-selected sample.
records.method: Caregiver-reported medication and symptom/diagnostic questionnaires; observational associations.
records.results: Overall 59% used psychotropic medication; 21% received multiple medicines. A Tourette diagnosis was among reported predictors of polypharmacy. The abstract does not provide the TS subgroup count, coefficient, interval or complete adjustment model. Only 5/231 received at least three medication classes, limiting inference.
records.limitations: Confounding by indication, caregiving and diagnostic ascertainment remain possible. No untreated causal comparison, TS-specific medication-effect estimate or adverse-event rate is established. Do not extrapolate to all children with TS or severe persistent adults.
records.decision: Historical care-burden context, not new efficacy or safety evidence. No treatment change. No participant-level records accessed.

records.evidence_type: peer-reviewed systematic review/meta-analysis, secondary evidence, abstract-only extraction
records.results: The review describes trivial-to-no randomized cannabinoid benefit for TS and predominantly very-low-certainty evidence overall. Increased THC adverse-event withdrawals are pooled across the review, not established as TS-specific.
records.limitations: TS-specific trial denominators, pooled effect and uncertainty are absent from the inspected abstract. Reviews reuse primary cohorts and must not be counted as additional participants or an independent efficacy replication.
records.decision: Historical counterevidence lead only. Inspect lawful primary TS trial aggregates before any new quantitative comparison; no treatment recommendation.
